advisory.finding: Re-pinning identity.enforce_since forward (from 8dcef776... to 0cf8c035..., the current tracker HEAD) moves every mutating event introduced in the window between the old and new anchors out of ENFORCED scope and into permanently-grandfathered scope, so any unsigned/forged/unverified non-exempt authored event that landed in that window is silently exempted from the authenticated-authorship gate. Nothing validates that the new anchor is not advanced past genuinely-unverified events; the anchor is fully config-trusted and _is_enforced() trusts since_ref wholesale.
merged_from: The enforce_since comment claims the anchor grandfathers 'the remediation's own tracking-ticket writes', but under the gate's strict-ancestor semantics any event whose introducing commit IS the anchor or a descendant is ENFORCED, not grandfathered — so this change's own rebar-ticket writes (which land at/after the anchor) are enforced, not exempted. The mismatch does not weaken the gate (it enforces more) but the documented rationale is incorrect and could mislead a future operator re-pinning the anchor.
scenarios: An unsigned or wrong-key authored (non-exempt) event was committed to the tickets branch between 8dcef776 and 0cf8c035; after this change it is grandfathered and the gate reports 0 enforced-not-verified even though that event is never authorship-verified
A future re-pin of enforce_since to a later HEAD becomes a standing pattern to clear a red gate by grandfathering rather than by signing/fixing
